name: Edgewater
title: Edgewater Window Cleaning, Water View Glass | CleanzATX
description: Window cleaning for Edgewater in Lakeway, with larger homes and water views from 2,200 to 4,800 square feet. Outside windows $10 each. Text for a quote.
intro: Edgewater is a Lakeway neighborhood of larger homes, some with water views. CleanzATX handles view glass with a pure water system that dries without streaks.

paragraphs: Homes in Edgewater run from about 2,200 to 4,800 square feet and sell between $700K and $1.7M. Some have water views, which raises both the price and the importance of the windows. There is no gate, and we know of no association here.

The wide price range tells you that the neighborhood has both mid sized family homes and bigger houses built around a view. Owners with a view tend to take the biggest interest in the glass, since it frames what they see every day.

Near the water, humidity and spray can leave a mineral film. Sprinklers do the same on lawns. Over several seasons that film builds, and glass looks hazy even after a rinse. Left alone for years, it can etch. Cedar pollen in winter and live oak pollen in spring add a yellow layer.

Facing the water usually means facing the sun for part of the day. Streaks show easily on west glass in late afternoon. A squeegee finish can leave faint lines, but a water fed pole with near 0 TDS water lets glass dry with no lines or film. Removal of old mineral spots is $10 per pane.

Setting up a visit is simple. There is no gate, so we park and start. Poles reach second and third story glass from the ground, which matters on lots that slope toward the water. Inside, we squeegee by hand and put drop cloths under each window. Many view homes add a deck or patio cleaning by hand, and a house soft wash to clear algae from humid siding and stucco.

A 3,500 square foot Edgewater home is about $350 for the exterior, with about three hours outside. A 4,800 square foot house comes to about $480. Adding the inside is another 90 minutes to two and a half hours depending on size.

faq.q: Why does my view glass look hazy?
faq.a: Haze usually comes from mineral film left by lake humidity and sprinkler water. Regular cleaning removes it, and old buildup can be treated at $10 per pane.

faq.q: Can you reach high windows on a slope?
faq.a: Yes. Water fed poles reach up to three stories from level ground, so we do not need to place ladders on slopes.

faq.q: How much for a home with a view?
faq.a: Exterior windows run about $0.10 per square foot. A 4,000 square foot house comes to roughly $400. Interior plus exterior is priced at $15 per window.

faq.q: Do you clean decks and patios too?
faq.a: Yes. Patios and decks are cleaned by hand so water stays controlled. Concrete flatwork is priced at $0.18 per square foot, with a $250 minimum.

faq.q: What is the best plan for a view home?
faq.a: Quarterly takes 15% off and includes a yearly free screen cleaning, hard water removal on up to 5 windows each visit and the 7 day rain guarantee.
